tiers.name: Part I: Key News & Developments
tiers.description: Macro economy, politics, social security, international relations, industry and key client movements in Paraguay

tiers.name: Part II: Analysis & Recommendations
tiers.description: Enterprise impact assessment and China-specific strategic recommendations

events.title: BCP holds policy rate at 5.50% and raises the 2026 growth forecast to 5.0% (2026-10-30)
events.summary: The Central Bank's Monetary Policy Committee kept the policy rate at 5.50% and reaffirmed a neutral stance, with annual inflation at 1.7% in September (monthly 0.1%, core 1.5%) and activity growing 6.7% year-on-year in August as measured by the IMAEP. The BCP raised its 2026 GDP growth projection from 4.5% to 5.0%, driven by services, electricity and water, and cut its end-2026 inflation forecast from 3.3% to 3.0%, with the core forecast lowered from 2.8% to 2.2%. Medium-term expectations remain anchored at 3.5%. The committee flagged external risks from Middle East geopolitical tensions, energy prices and higher US rates, and set the next meeting for 20 November. Stable rates and strong activity support domestic demand, credit and telecom/data consumption.

events.title: Guaraní rebounds as government and business groups set up a permanent FX technical table (2026-10-30)
events.summary: After several sessions of gains the dollar retreated again, closing around G. 5,750 bid and G. 5,900 offered in the retail market, while the interbank rate stood near G. 5,912–5,945. The guaraní has appreciated about 11% year-to-date, 17% year-on-year and 28% since April 2025, when the dollar peaked at G. 8,006. Exporters, real-estate and productive sectors warn that the strong currency cuts guaraní revenue and competitiveness. The National Economic Team and business guilds installed a permanent technical table to design exchange-rate predictability mechanisms, while the Senate requested reports from the BCP on the fall and its intervention criteria. The debate raises the risk of policy responses that could alter the current free-float framework.

events.title: Bicameral budget committee keeps PGN 2027 at G. 166.3tn and reallocates G. 185.7bn (2026-10-29)
events.summary: The Congressional Bicameral Budget Committee issued its dictamen on the 2027 national budget, keeping the global amount at G. 166.3 trillion (about USD 25.7 billion) and approving reallocations of G. 185,745.7 million (around USD 28.7 million) financed by a cut in the debt-repayment reprogramming. The text includes a G. 500,000 monthly increase for 28,691 public-health workers from July 2027 and additional funds for the Labour Ministry, the MEF (severance for former Acepar workers), the Public Defender's Office, Diben, Senadis, public universities and indigenous education. The project still carries a 3.9%-of-GDP deficit and an exceptional waiver of the Fiscal Responsibility Law. It now goes to the Chamber of Deputies, which scheduled the article-by-article debate for 9 November.

events.title: Paraguay spent more on mobile phones than on cars or diesel as China reaches 36.4% of imports (2026-10-28)
events.summary: BCP data for January–September show smartphone imports of USD 1,045.2 million, more than the value of imported automobiles or diesel, although phone purchases grew only 2.4% in value. Electrical machinery reached USD 477.6 million (+51.2%) and notebooks USD 428.2 million (+53.9%), the fastest-growing category. Total imports rose 15% to USD 15,260 million, with China supplying USD 5,447.6 million, or 36.4% of the total and 22.4% more than a year earlier, far ahead of Brazil (21.3%) and the United States (6.7%). Paraguay recorded a USD 712 million trade surplus, reversing last year's USD 555 million deficit. The figures underline both resilient consumer demand and the depth of Chinese supply chains despite the absence of diplomatic relations.

events.title: Bicameral deliberates the 2027 budget behind closed doors and removes journalists (2026-10-26)
events.summary: The Bicameral Budget Committee declared its 26 October deliberative session secret and asked journalists to leave the room while it debated an executive addendum of G. 398,778 million (about USD 61.7 million), mainly for salary increases in Education and Health. The decision drew criticism from press associations and opposition legislators, who argued that a budget affecting all citizens should be debated publicly. The committee had completed sector hearings in October, including the MEF, DNIT, TSJE, Supreme Court and Public Ministry. Three days later it issued its dictamen keeping the G. 166.3 trillion total. The episode signals a more contentious and less transparent budget process ahead of the 9 November debate in the Chamber of Deputies.

events.title: Cartes pulls his loyalists from Peña's bloc and forms an independent Honor Colorado bench (2026-10-28)
events.summary: Horacio Cartes removed several loyal senators and deputies — including Antonio 'Tony' Barrios, Gustavo Leite and Lizarella Valiente — from the congressional bloc aligned with President Santiago Peña and set up a separate Honor Colorado mini-bench. The move follows the withdrawal of Cartes's chosen presidential candidate, Juan Carlos Baruja, on 18 October and Cartes's decision not to seek re-election as ANR party president. Senator Varela warned that Peña has lost his 'hard and captive' Senate majority, forcing the Executive to negotiate support case by case, while Liberal opposition legislators see a better opening for 2028. The split does not remove Peña from office but fragments the ruling party's legislative machine ahead of budget and appointment votes.

events.title: New prison director unveils a 30/60/90-day plan to regain control after the Emboscada escape (2026-10-30)
events.summary: The new director of the prison system, Óscar Pereira, announced a plan to recover control of Paraguay's penitentiaries, with assessments at 30, 60 and 90 days, tighter controls, administrative investigations and measures to prevent internal complicity. The plan follows the escape of inmates from the Emboscada 'Martín Mendoza' penitentiary and comes amid changes at the Ministry of Justice. Pereira said responsibilities will be investigated and that security protocols will be reinforced. The episode adds to a broader security debate that includes organised crime, drug trafficking and the year-end police operation, and could trigger further institutional reshuffles in the justice and interior sectors.

events.title: Biochemists announce a second 10-day national strike after a G. 500,000 offer (2026-10-30)
events.summary: The Union of Biochemists of Paraguay ended a three-day strike in some 177 public laboratories and announced a second, 10-day national strike after the government offered only a G. 500,000 adjustment. The guild is demanding a G. 2,000,000 increase, supplies and appointments, saying salaries have been frozen for 14 years at G. 3.6 million for contract staff and G. 4.3 million for appointed staff, a 77% loss of purchasing power. The dispute is part of a wider health-sector wage conflict that includes doctors, nurses and administrative staff, and it increases pressure on the 2027 budget while disrupting laboratory services for public hospitals.

events.title: Health unions press the MEF for a 2027 budget addendum for 4,300 nurses and 10,000 workers (2026-10-29)
events.summary: Doctors and nurses convened by Sinadips protested outside the Ministry of Economy and Finance to demand a budget addendum to the 2027 PGN that includes a minimum salary band for 4,300 contracted nurses, who earn about G. 2.7 million, below the minimum wage, and an adjustment for some 10,000 health workers. The Intergremial de Salud is separately seeking a 50% salary recomposition for nearly 26,000 public-health employees, a measure it estimates would cost USD 140 million. The protests follow a tent installation outside the MEF on 24 October and feed directly into the Bicameral budget negotiations, where legislators already added a G. 500,000 raise for 28,691 health workers from July 2027.

events.title: Unemployment falls to 4.1% in Q3 as employment reaches 3.29 million (2026-10-30)
events.summary: The National Statistics Institute reported unemployment of 4.1% in July–September 2026, unchanged from the previous quarter but down 0.8 percentage points from 4.9% a year earlier. There were 141,250 unemployed people, 24,176 fewer than in the same period of 2025; female unemployment fell from 6.3% to 4.7%, while male unemployment edged down from 3.8% to 3.7%. The employment rate reached 70%, with 3,290,206 people employed, 66,149 more year-on-year, concentrated in commerce, restaurants and hotels. Urban unemployment was 4.4% and rural 3.2%; underemployment rose slightly to 4.2%, or 143,181 people. President Peña called the result a historic record, though informality and underemployment remain structural challenges.

events.title: Police launch an early Año Paha operation to protect banks and shops (2026-10-27)
events.summary: The National Police launched a special security device ahead of the year-end Año Paha season, with controls at vulnerable points, tactical personnel, Grupo Lince motorised patrols, explosives specialists and snipers in patrol cars. Reinforcements were announced for Central, Alto Paraná, Amambay, Canindeyú and Asunción, and 5,000 new officers are due to graduate on 18 December. The operation was triggered by an attempted ATM robbery in San Lorenzo and aims to protect banks, shops, cash machines and commercial corridors. It reflects both the seasonal rise in armed robbery and the political salience of citizen security ahead of the 2027 municipal and party calendar.

events.title: Ammonia leak at the Pollpar chicken plant affects 48 workers (2026-10-30)
events.summary: An ammonia leak at the Pollpar S.A. chicken-processing plant in Mariano Roque Alonso affected about 48 people, according to the company and health authorities. Thirty workers were treated at the IPS Central Hospital and 18 at the Yrendague clinic; most were discharged, while four women remained under observation with oxygen. The Labour Ministry and the IPS opened investigations into the cause and into safety conditions at the plant. The incident highlights occupational-safety gaps in Paraguay's food-processing and cold-chain sector, where ammonia refrigeration is common, and may prompt tighter inspections of industrial facilities near Asunción.

events.title: Peña congratulates Lula on his Brazil runoff victory and pledges to keep working together (2026-10-26)
events.summary: President Santiago Peña congratulated Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva after his victory over Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's 25 October runoff, saying the two countries share an integration and development agenda and will keep working together. Paraguay joined most right-leaning South American governments in recognising the result, with Argentina's Javier Milei the notable exception. The outcome shifts attention back to the Itaipú Annex C review and the tariff of USD 19.28 per kW-month that expires in December 2026. Analysts argue Lula has historically been more responsive to Paraguayan demands, but he will face a difficult Congress; Peña had avoided endorsing either candidate during the campaign.

events.title: Díaz-Balart highlights the US–Paraguay strategic alliance in security and technology (2026-10-27)
events.summary: US Congressman Mario Díaz-Balart stressed the strategic alliance between Washington and Asunción in security and technology, citing Paraguay's accession to the Pax Silica initiative as its 26th partner, its critical minerals and hydroelectric resources for AI infrastructure, and the new INL anti-narcotics office in Asunción as a regional hub for the Southern Cone. His remarks followed the 19–21 October visit of Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, the signing of air-interception and border-security instruments, and the announcement of USD 11.75 million in security assistance. The alignment deepens US investment and intelligence cooperation but also raises Paraguay's exposure to US–China technology competition.

events.title: Paraguay, Bolivia and Uruguay strengthen Urupabol cooperation in Asunción (2026-10-30)
events.summary: Foreign ministers and officials from Paraguay, Bolivia and Uruguay met in Asunción under the Urupabol group, chaired by Paraguayan Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano, to strengthen regional cooperation. The agenda covered logistics and port integration, navigability of the Paraguay–Paraná Hidrovía, air connectivity, multimodal corridors and productive, commercial and energy integration. For landlocked Paraguay, the group is a complementary platform to Mercosur for reducing export logistics costs and improving access to Atlantic and Pacific routes. The meeting produced no binding commitments but reinforces Asunción's push for infrastructure coordination ahead of the 2027–2028 election cycle.

events.title: Paraguayan firms join the fourth Mercosur–EU business round in Resistencia (2026-10-29)
events.summary: More than 250 companies, including a Paraguayan delegation, took part in the fourth Mercosur–EU business round in Resistencia, Chaco, Argentina, focused on food for supermarkets, construction and wood, trade, services, software and the knowledge economy. The interim Mercosur–EU trade agreement has applied provisionally since 1 May 2026, and the government estimates that at least 95% of Paraguay's current and potential exports will enter Europe tariff-free or with preferences. The main unresolved issue is the internal distribution of quotas: Paraguay is asking for 25%, while Uruguay and Argentina want allocation based on historical trade and Brazil on global trade. A five-year phase-in and certification requirements will determine how quickly firms can use the preferences.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI

events.title: Paraguay to host a USD 12bn AI campus after joining Pax Silica (2026-10-30)
events.summary: Paraguay is set to host 'Iguazú AI City', a data-centre campus in Yguazú, Alto Paraná, developed by US-based Crusoe and Paraguayan Araico, with a headline investment of USD 12 billion over its first three years, equivalent to roughly a quarter of GDP, and about 280 MW of contracted demand. Phase 1 is only 6 MW and around USD 300 million, with commissioning targeted for late 2026 or early 2027; Phase 2 adds 130 MW and USD 5.5 billion in Q2 2028, and Phase 3 a similar amount in 2029. Power is priced at USD 45/MWh at 220 kV with annual indexation, and capacity will be sold through Crusoe Cloud from Q1 2027. The project was showcased after Paraguay became the 26th Pax Silica partner.

events.title: Energy expert warns of a 2030–31 supply crunch and calls Annex C renegotiation a 'utopia' (2026-10-29)
events.summary: Former ANDE manager and energy specialist Fabián Cáceres warned that Paraguay will face severe supply problems around 2030–2031 and may need to import electricity from Brazil, because domestic consumption is approaching the combined output of Itaipú, Yacyretá and Acaray while no new generation tenders are under way and transmission infrastructure is outdated. He called a full renegotiation of Itaipú's Annex C a 'utopia' and said Paraguay 'missed the train', since rising domestic demand will soon absorb its share. He also warned that the country committed 286 MW to a data-centre developer without knowing the final 2027 energy price, and urged a single command unit plus bilateral deals with Brazil. The current USD 19.28/kW-month tariff expires in December 2026.

events.title: Expiry of ANDE's Itaipú operating agreement threatens cheap surplus energy (2026-10-29)
events.summary: The operating agreement that allows ANDE to access cheap surplus energy from Itaipú expires at the end of 2026, and its loss could significantly affect the state utility's finances and eventually consumer tariffs. Paraguay consumed 25,768 GWh from Itaipú in 2025, 26.4% more than the previous year, while still ceding about a quarter of its half of the output to Brazil. The expiry coincides with the Annex C review, the new USD 45–49/MWh tariff for electro-intensive data-centre clients and rising demand from AI projects. If the surplus mechanism disappears before new generation and transmission come online, ANDE may have to buy replacement power at higher cost, weakening the case for energy-intensive investment.

events.title: Conatel closes the public consultation on the 2026–2030 National Telecom Plan (2026-10-26)
events.summary: Conatel closed the public consultation on the draft National Telecommunications Plan 2026–2030, extending the deadline to 26 October. The plan rests on three pillars: infrastructure and coverage, service quality, and affordability and digital inclusion. Targets for 2030 include 265 districts connected to a fibre backbone, 95.6% population coverage for 4G and 30% for 5G, average mobile download speeds of 35 Mbps and fixed speeds of 160 Mbps, 80% fibre in fixed connections, 60% of homes with fixed access and a 40% reduction in the average price per mobile gigabyte. Estimated capex is USD 2.313 billion, including USD 113 million for a 5,543 km backbone. The final plan will shape spectrum, IoT and homologation rules and the next tender pipeline.

events.title: Claro's 5G network reaches 27 cities and 3 million people (2026-10-29)
events.summary: Claro Paraguay's 5G network now covers 27 cities across 10 departments, with potential coverage for more than 3 million people, and the operator expects to exceed 100 operational sites by the end of 2026. The rollout began in 2025 with 12 strategic localities covering the central area and has since added Coronel Oviedo, Villarrica, Pedro Juan Caballero, Hernandarias, Ciudad del Este, Encarnación and Cambyretá. Independent nPerf measurements in September still showed national 5G coverage of 23.75%, heavily concentrated in Asunción (77.7%), indicating that marketing coverage and real user experience remain far apart. Claro is positioning itself as the 5G coverage leader before Tigo and Personal launch in early 2027.

events.title: Personal launches a SIM Swap API to fight SIM-swap fraud (2026-10-30)
events.summary: Personal Empresas launched SIM Swap, an API that lets banks, fintechs and merchants verify in real time when a customer's SIM card was last changed, in order to prevent SIM-swapping fraud. The service adds identity checks and is designed to help regulated clients comply with the Central Bank's Communication 'A' 7783 on digital security. The launch shows Personal moving beyond connectivity into B2B digital-trust services, a segment with higher margins and stickiness than consumer data. For technology suppliers, it signals demand for subscriber-data integration, API gateways, fraud analytics and security orchestration layered on top of the mobile core.

events.title: Personal's CEO warns of a 'perfect storm' and pitches Telco for AI with 13 data centres (2026-10-28)
events.summary: Roberto Nobile, CEO of Personal and Telecom Argentina, told a regional panel that telecommunications faces a 'perfect storm': flat or falling revenue per user against heavy fibre and 5G Standalone investment, with AI-driven traffic growth set to turn the investment gap into a capacity gap. He said more than 75% of mobile traffic is generated by a few hyperscalers that do not bear capacity costs, and proposed consolidation, fair-share contributions, symmetric regulation, network slicing for enterprise customers and a 'Telco for AI' strategy built on the group's 13 data centres. The agenda matters for Paraguay because Personal must launch 5G by February 2027 and is weighing where to invest in edge and AI infrastructure.

events.title: Millicom (Tigo) schedules third-quarter results for 5 November (2026-10-28)
events.summary: Millicom, the parent of Tigo Paraguay, announced that it will publish third-quarter 2026 results on 5 November, followed by a video conference for the financial community. Consensus revenue is around USD 2.23 billion at group level, although Paraguay is not reported separately. The results will be watched for capex guidance as Tigo prepares to launch 5G in the 2.3 GHz band by February 2027, with a commitment to at least 100 radio bases within four years and a joint USD 80 million programme with Personal. Any upgrade in group capex or commentary on fibre and data-centre opportunities would be a leading indicator for 2027 vendor orders in Paraguay.

sections.title: VII. Integrated Impact Analysis for Business
sections.impact_analysis:
🟡 The exchange rate is now the main macro-policy fault line. The guaraní closed around G. 5,945 per dollar on the BCP's 30 October planilla, after appreciating roughly 11% year-to-date and 17% year-on-year, and the government and business guilds have created a permanent technical table to discuss predictability. A stronger guaraní lowers the local-currency cost of imported network equipment and handsets, but it squeezes exporters and local partners and raises the risk of administrative or quasi-fiscal responses. Contracts should be denominated or indexed in USD, with explicit FX clauses and scenario planning for a move back toward G. 6,100–6,200 if seasonal dollar supply fades.

🟢 The real economy remains supportive. The BCP held the policy rate at 5.50% on 30 October, raised its 2026 growth forecast to 5.0% and cut end-2026 inflation to 3.0%, while INE reported unemployment at 4.1% and employment at 3.29 million. Stable rates, low inflation and record employment support consumer demand for connectivity, smartphones and digital services. The caveat is that growth is increasingly services-led and that underemployment (4.2%) and informality limit disposable-income gains in the interior, where 5G monetisation is weakest.

🔴 Fiscal rigidities are building. The Bicameral budget committee kept the 2027 PGN at G. 166.3 trillion with a 3.9%-of-GDP deficit and an exceptional waiver of the Fiscal Responsibility Law, while adding a G. 398.8 billion salary addendum debated in a closed session and reallocating G. 185.7 billion from debt repayment. Tax revenue grew only 2.3% through September against an 8% target, and the state still owes large arrears to health suppliers and MOPC contractors. Public-sector ICT, energy and infrastructure projects face payment-delay and renegotiation risk, so exposure to ANDE, MOPC and health entities should be secured or avoided.

🟡 Politics is more fragmented but not unstable. Cartes's decision to pull his loyalists into an independent Honor Colorado bench weakens Peña's captive Senate majority and makes budget, appointments and reform votes case-by-case. The 2028 succession fight will absorb legislative bandwidth, while the government's US alignment (Pax Silica, INL office, USD 11.75 million security package) remains one of the few stable axes. For investors, the practical effect is slower decision-making and more need for local political intelligence, not an immediate policy rupture.

🔴 Energy is the biggest structural risk to the data-centre story. The Itaipú operating agreement expires at the end of 2026, the USD 19.28/kW-month tariff is due for revision, and experts warn of a 2030–31 supply crunch. The USD 12 billion Iguazú AI City project is real but back-loaded: Phase 1 is only 6 MW and about USD 300 million, with 97.5% of the headline dependent on later phases, ANDE tariff treatment and the Annex C outcome. Data-centre demand is a genuine opportunity for power equipment, cooling, fibre and ICT, but suppliers should underwrite phase-by-phase and avoid treating the headline number as committed capex.

🟢 Telecom capex is entering a new cycle. Conatel's 2026–2030 plan targets 30% 5G population coverage and USD 2.313 billion of investment, Claro already claims 27 cities and 3 million people covered, and Tigo and Personal must activate 5G by February 2027 with at least 100 sites each within four years. At the same time, the 5G tenders retain trusted-vendor restrictions that disadvantage Chinese equipment, and Nubicom's weak commercial performance (two subscribers after 34 sites) shows that licences do not guarantee viable demand. The winners will be vendors that combine radio access, fibre, energy efficiency and local integration rather than box sales alone.

🔴 The China angle cuts both ways. China supplied 36.4% of Paraguay's imports in January–September (USD 5.45 billion), and smartphones alone were a USD 1.05 billion category, so Chinese supply chains remain indispensable. But Asunción recognizes Taiwan, Beijing sanctioned MITIC minister Gustavo Villate in October, and the US is tying investment and security cooperation to technology alignment. Chinese firms should keep a low political profile, document compliance, avoid dual-use exposure and use Mercosur–EU rules of origin and local assembly where possible to diversify market access.

sections.title: VIII. Targeted Recommendations for Chinese Enterprises
sections.impact_analysis:
🟡 Make FX a first-order commercial term. With the guaraní near G. 5,945 and appreciation of about 11% year-to-date, price contracts in USD or index them to the BCP rate, shorten payment terms for guaraní-denominated receivables and stress-test a rebound to G. 6,100–6,200. The government–guild technical table could produce intervention or tax measures; monitor BCP communications and Senate requests rather than assuming the free float continues unchanged.

🟢 Build a 5G and fibre pipeline, not a one-off tender strategy. Conatel's 2026–2030 plan envisages USD 2.313 billion of capex, 265 districts with fibre backbone and 30% 5G population coverage by 2030; Claro plans more than 100 sites by end-2026, and Tigo and Personal must launch by February 2027 and reach 100 sites each within four years. Engage early with operators on engineering, Open RAN, energy-efficient radio and fibre backhaul, and partner with local integrators to navigate trusted-vendor rules. Position as a multi-vendor, standards-compliant supplier rather than a single-box vendor.

🟢 Target the data-centre supply chain, but underwrite it phase by phase. The Iguazú AI City headline is USD 12 billion and 280 MW, yet Phase 1 is only 6 MW and about USD 300 million, and the 286 MW ANDE PPA price is not yet settled for 2027. Focus on Phase 1 and 2 equipment—UPS, cooling, switchgear, prefabricated modules, fibre and DCIM—and require milestone-based payment, performance guarantees and clarity on the ANDE tariff and Annex C before scaling. Avoid inventory or capacity commitments based on the full headline.

🔴 Protect public-sector cash flow. The 2027 budget carries a 3.9%-of-GDP deficit and a Fiscal Responsibility Law waiver, revenue is running at 2.3% versus an 8% target, and arrears to health suppliers and MOPC contractors are large. For ANDE, MOPC, health and municipal projects, require sovereign or multilateral guarantees, escrow or milestone payments, and monitor the 9 November Deputy debate and subsequent Senate vote. Do not assume the PGN will be executed as approved.

🟡 Manage political and sanctions risk deliberately. Paraguay's Taiwan recognition and the October sanctions on MITIC minister Gustavo Villate show that technology issues can become diplomatic ones; US pressure on trusted vendors and cyber-security accusations add friction. Keep a low public profile, strengthen compliance and export-control screening, use local counsel and avoid staffing projects with personnel exposed to visa or sanctions risk. Where possible, localise assembly or services to create Paraguayan jobs and political cover.

🟢 Use Mercosur–EU and Urupabol channels for market access. The interim Mercosur–EU agreement has applied since May 2026 and covers at least 95% of Paraguayan exports at zero or preferential tariffs, while the Urupabol meeting focused on Hidrovía, port and multimodal integration. For projects with regional content, design rules-of-origin-compliant supply chains and consider Paraguay as a light assembly or distribution base for Mercosur, while monitoring the unresolved quota allocation (Paraguay is asking for 25%).

🟡 Plan for social and security disruption. Health-sector strikes (biochemists' 10-day walkout, nurses' protests), the Emboscada prison escape and the early Año Paha police operation can disrupt logistics, site access and public-services payment. Maintain security protocols for staff and warehouses, build buffer stock for Q4, and avoid relying on public laboratories or health facilities for project timelines.
